analysis:
The code snippet calls `tables.toArray(new String[tables.size()])`. The `tables` variable is a `Set<String>` (specifically `HashSet`). The argument to `toArray` is a newly created `String` array of the same size as the set. The API documentation lists two exceptions: `NullPointerException` if the specified array is null, and `ArrayStoreException` if the runtime type of the specified array is not a supertype of every element in the set. In this context:
- `NullPointerException`: The array is created with `new String[tables.size()]`, which is non-null, so this exception is avoided.
- `ArrayStoreException`: The array type is `String[]`, and the set contains only `String` elements (since the code adds strings from `names` and `mViewTables.get(lowercase)` to a `Set<String>`). The runtime type `String` is a supertype of itself, so all elements are compatible. Thus this exception is also avoided.

Therefore, both declared exceptions are fully avoided by the calling context.
answer: Both declared exceptions (NullPointerException and ArrayStoreException) are avoided.
remark: No exceptions are triggered because the array argument is non-null (avoiding NullPointerException) and its runtime type (`String[]`) is a supertype of all elements in the set (which are all strings), thus avoiding ArrayStoreException.
